grammar: Word order: subject, verb, object. With one participant: subject, verb.
A separate word before the noun phrase, marking the instrument, the thing used (“with a spear”).
A separate word before the noun phrase, marking a companion, someone doing it alongside (“with the queen”).
On the verb when the subject is plural.
Come after the noun. Noun endings go on the noun only; the adjective stays bare.
Go at the end of the sentence.
